original_poem:
எண்ணும் இசைமயமாக் கம்பனெழுதின 
மண்ணே யொன்றும் சேராதே.
நண்ணும் வரவான கங்கை 
பட்டுயர்தருமென்றே.
translated_poem:
Kambar wrote in music’s sweet rhythm,
Yet, none on this earth shall unite.
The Ganges, in its essence,
Will not dwell in the land of delight.

stanzas.loss_note: இசைமயமாக் (isaimayamaak) refers to the specific musical prosody of Kamban's Iramavataram, the pinnacle of classical Tamil literary achievement; 'music's sweet rhythm' preserves surface sound but loses the technical weight of Tamil metrical tradition, and மண்ணே யொன்றும் சேராதே carries a philosophical resignation absent in the translation.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the unreachable sacred beyond Tamil civilisational reach

cultural_entities.translation_note: Kamban is named and retained, but his status as the supreme poet of Tamil literary tradition is not conveyed.
The technical Tamil prosodic concept of isai-mayam is rendered as generic 'music's sweet rhythm', losing its classical literary-metrical specificity.
The Ganges is named, but its role as a contrast to the Kaveri in Tamil sacred geography is lost.
